topics.title: Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming
topics.description: What OOP is and why it exists: objects with state, behaviour and identity, message passing, the four pillars, and how OOP differs from procedural code.

topics.title: Classes and Objects
topics.description: Class vs object vs reference, object creation, default values, aliasing, pass-by-value of references, the this keyword and anonymous objects.

topics.title: Constructors and Initialization
topics.description: Constructor rules, default and copy constructors, this() and super() chaining, instance and static initializer blocks, and full initialization order.

topics.title: Static Members
topics.description: Static fields and methods, why static code has no this, static vs instance members, method hiding, static calls through null, and when to avoid static.

topics.title: Object Lifecycle and Memory
topics.description: The stack and heap model, GC roots and reachability, eligibility for garbage collection, finalize vs try-with-resources, and memory leaks in Java.

topics.title: Encapsulation
topics.description: Data hiding, the four access modifiers, getters and setters done right, validation, invariants, defensive copying, JavaBeans, and refactoring leaky classes.

topics.title: Inheritance
topics.description: extends and IS-A, inheritance types, why Java has no multiple class inheritance, super, field and method hiding, final, and the fragile base class problem.

topics.title: Polymorphism
topics.description: Compile-time vs runtime polymorphism, dynamic method dispatch, static vs dynamic binding, and what the compiler knows versus what the runtime object is.

topics.title: Method Overloading
topics.description: Valid overloads, how the compiler picks one (widening, boxing, varargs, most specific), null and ambiguous calls, and overloading across a class hierarchy.

topics.title: Method Overriding
topics.description: Overriding rules for signature, covariant returns, access and checked exceptions; @Override; and why static, private and final methods are not overridden.

topics.title: Upcasting and Downcasting
topics.description: Implicit upcasts, explicit downcasts, compile-time and runtime cast checks, instanceof and pattern matching, and array covariance vs generic invariance.

topics.title: Abstraction
topics.description: Hiding implementation behind contracts: abstract classes and methods with their rules, levels of abstraction, and abstraction compared with encapsulation.

topics.title: Interfaces
topics.description: Interface members by Java version, default-method conflict rules, static and private methods, functional and marker interfaces, and abstract class vs interface.

topics.title: Association, Aggregation and Composition
topics.description: Association with multiplicity and navigability, aggregation vs composition by ownership and lifecycle, dependency, IS-A vs HAS-A, and UML notation.

topics.title: Composition over Inheritance
topics.description: Why HAS-A plus delegation usually beats IS-A for reuse, refactoring a subclass hierarchy into composed policies, and when inheritance is still right.

topics.title: The Object Class
topics.description: Methods every class inherits from Object, identity vs logical equality, == vs equals with strings and wrapper caching, toString, getClass, and clone pitfalls.

topics.title: equals() and hashCode()
topics.description: The equals and hashCode contracts, how HashMap uses both, what breaks when one is missing, mutable keys, symmetry with subclasses, and compareTo consistency.

topics.title: Immutability
topics.description: Why immutable objects matter, final reference vs immutable object, String and wrapper immutability, a step-by-step immutable class, unmodifiable vs immutable, records.

topics.title: Java-Specific OOP
topics.description: Core OOP concepts mapped to Java mechanisms and rules: static, final and abstract, final vs finally vs finalize, this and super, and virtual-by-default methods.

topics.title: Nested Classes
topics.description: Static nested, inner, local and anonymous classes: how to create each, Outer.this, captured variables, anonymous classes vs lambdas, and inner-class leaks.

topics.title: Modern Java OOP Features: Enums, Records and Sealed Classes
topics.description: Enums with fields and behaviour, records and compact constructors, sealed hierarchies with permits/final/non-sealed, and pattern matching for instanceof.

topics.title: Binding and Method Resolution
topics.description: How the compiler selects a method signature and the JVM finds its implementation: static vs dynamic binding, with ten progressively harder output examples.

topics.title: OOP with Collections
topics.description: How collections depend on equals, hashCode and compareTo; Comparable vs Comparator; TreeSet and TreeMap duplicate rules; and mutating objects inside collections.

topics.title: OOP with Generics
topics.description: Generic classes, interfaces and methods, bounded type parameters, wildcards and PECS, generic invariance, type erasure, and generics in OOP design.

topics.title: OOP with Exceptions
topics.description: Exceptions as objects in a class hierarchy, checked vs unchecked, custom exception design, exception translation and chaining, and good vs bad handling.

topics.title: OOP with Multithreading
topics.description: Designing thread-safe classes: shared mutable state, encapsulating locks, compound actions, immutable snapshots, composition pitfalls and deadlock-free design.

topics.title: OOP with Testing
topics.description: What makes classes testable, arrange-act-assert, injecting collaborators and clocks, stubs, fakes, spies and mocks, and how SOLID supports testing.

topics.title: SOLID Principles
topics.description: The five SOLID principles in one place: what each means, how they reinforce each other, how patterns apply them, and how to use them without overengineering.

topics.title: Single Responsibility Principle
topics.description: One reason to change per class: spotting mixed responsibilities, splitting an invoice class by concern, and avoiding over-splitting and anaemic models.

topics.title: Open/Closed Principle
topics.description: Open for extension, closed for modification: replacing type switches with abstractions, the ways Java achieves OCP, and avoiding speculative extension points.

topics.title: Liskov Substitution Principle
topics.description: Subtypes must honour the base contract: preconditions, postconditions, invariants, the Square-Rectangle problem, refused bequests and contract tests.

topics.title: Interface Segregation Principle
topics.description: Clients should not depend on methods they do not use: splitting a fat payment interface into role interfaces, and splitting by client need without over-splitting.

topics.title: Dependency Inversion Principle
topics.description: High-level policy and low-level details both depend on abstractions owned by the policy; DIP vs DI vs IoC; and where inversion pays off.

topics.title: Coupling and Cohesion
topics.description: Kinds of coupling and cohesion, why low coupling and high cohesion go together, and how interfaces, injection and composition loosen tightly coupled code.

topics.title: Dependency Injection and Inversion of Control
topics.description: Constructor, setter and field injection, why constructor injection is preferred, DI without a framework, IoC vs DI vs DIP, and how Spring fits in.

topics.title: Designing Classes from Requirements
topics.description: A ten-step process for turning a problem statement into classes: requirements, entities, responsibilities, relationships, abstractions, checks and scenarios.

topics.title: UML Class Diagrams
topics.description: Class boxes, visibility, association, aggregation, composition, inheritance, realization and dependency, multiplicity, object diagrams, and mapping UML to Java.

topics.title: Clean Code Principles for OOP
topics.description: Names, small classes and methods, parameter objects, boolean flags, defensive programming, Tell Don't Ask, Law of Demeter, DRY, KISS and YAGNI as principles.

topics.title: Code Smells and Refactoring
topics.description: Thirteen common OOP smells with their causes, and step-by-step refactorings with Java before-and-after code: extract, move, value objects, polymorphism, delegation.

topics.title: OOP Anti-Patterns
topics.description: Overused inheritance, deep hierarchies, singleton abuse, global state, anaemic models, god objects, excessive abstraction and premature or inappropriate patterns.

topics.title: Introduction to Design Patterns
topics.description: What design patterns are, the GoF creational/structural/behavioral categories, the principles behind them, interview priorities, and a problem-to-pattern map.

topics.title: Singleton
topics.description: One instance with global access: eager, lazy, synchronized, double-checked locking with volatile, holder idiom and enum singletons, plus testability problems.

topics.title: Factory Method
topics.description: Let subclasses decide which product to create through an overridable creation method; compared with simple factories and static factory methods.

topics.title: Abstract Factory
topics.description: Create consistent families of related objects through one factory interface, illustrated with country-specific tax and invoice components.

topics.title: Builder
topics.description: Assemble complex immutable objects step by step: telescoping constructors, the fluent static nested builder, validation in build(), and when not to use it.

topics.title: Prototype
topics.description: Create objects by copying configured prototypes through a copy method and registry, with shallow vs deep copying and why copy constructors beat clone().

topics.title: Adapter
topics.description: Make an incompatible existing class work through the interface your code expects, with object vs class adapters and wrapping vendor SDKs.

topics.title: Bridge
topics.description: Separate two independent dimensions of variation into two hierarchies joined by composition, avoiding subclass explosion.

topics.title: Composite
topics.description: Treat leaves and containers uniformly in part-whole trees, shown with nested product bundles, and where to declare child management.

topics.title: Decorator
topics.description: Add responsibilities dynamically by stacking same-interface wrappers: logging, caching and retry around a service, and java.io streams.

topics.title: Facade
topics.description: One simple entry point over a complex subsystem, shown with a checkout workflow, and how to keep a facade from becoming a god object.

topics.title: Flyweight
topics.description: Share immutable intrinsic state among huge numbers of objects, with a seat-map example and JDK caches such as Integer.valueOf and the string pool.

topics.title: Proxy
topics.description: Control access to an object through a same-interface surrogate: virtual, protection, remote, caching proxies, JDK dynamic proxies and Spring.

topics.title: Chain of Responsibility
topics.description: Pass a request along a configurable chain of handlers until one handles it, with expense approvals, servlet filters and pipeline variants.

topics.title: Command
topics.description: Encapsulate requests as objects for undo/redo, queuing and logging, with an inventory editor example and Runnable/Callable as JDK commands.

topics.title: Interpreter
topics.description: Represent a small grammar as classes and evaluate rule trees recursively, shown with combinable coupon-eligibility rules.

topics.title: Iterator
topics.description: Traverse a collection without exposing its structure: Iterable and Iterator, a custom date-range iterator, fail-fast behaviour and safe removal.

topics.title: Mediator
topics.description: Centralise how a group of objects interact so they no longer reference each other, shown with booking-screen components.

topics.title: Memento
topics.description: Save and restore an object's state through opaque snapshots without breaking encapsulation, with an exam answer-sheet checkpoint example.

topics.title: Observer
topics.description: Notify many observers when a subject changes: order events, push vs pull, sync vs async, failure isolation, unsubscription and Spring events.

topics.title: State
topics.description: Change an object's behaviour as its internal state changes, with an order lifecycle, default rejections, an enum alternative, and State vs Strategy.

topics.title: Strategy
topics.description: Interchangeable algorithms behind one interface, chosen at runtime: delivery-fee rules, lambdas as strategies, and Comparator in the JDK.

topics.title: Template Method
topics.description: Fix an algorithm's skeleton in a final method and let subclasses implement steps and hooks, shown with a data-import workflow.

topics.title: Visitor
topics.description: Add operations to a stable class hierarchy with double dispatch, shown with GST and shipping-weight visitors, and its trade-off with sealed types.

topics.title: Design Pattern Comparisons
topics.description: Side-by-side comparisons of look-alike patterns and a guide for choosing the right one from a problem description.

topics.title: Parking Lot Design
topics.description: Floors, typed spots, tickets and fees: fit rules in enums, allocation and pricing as strategies, and safe spot assignment under concurrency.

topics.title: Library Management System Design
topics.description: Books vs copies, members with loan limits, loans with due dates and fines, and a reservation queue that holds returned copies.

topics.title: Vehicle Rental System Design
topics.description: Branches, vehicle types with pricing strategies, date-range availability and booking without double booking.

topics.title: ATM Design
topics.description: An ATM session as a state machine, the bank behind an interface, and note planning that never debits before cash can be dispensed.

topics.title: Food Ordering System Design
topics.description: Single-restaurant carts, frozen order prices, status transitions, delivery-fee and partner-assignment strategies, and event notifications.

topics.title: OOP Interview Questions by Level
topics.description: Thirty Java OOP questions from beginner definitions to advanced design, each with a model answer and a question-style label.

topics.title: OOP Output-Based Questions
topics.description: Twenty verified Java programs testing constructor order, overloading, overriding, hiding, casting, defaults and equals/hashCode behaviour.

topics.title: OOP Scenario-Based Questions
topics.description: Realistic design scenarios: who owns a responsibility, inheritance or composition, which pattern and why, with reasoned answers.

topics.title: OOP Interview Traps
topics.description: Twenty-two statements that sound right but are wrong, from inherited constructors and overridden statics to final lists and singletons.

topics.title: "Why?" Questions in OOP
topics.description: Reasoning questions such as why no multiple class inheritance, why equals and hashCode must agree, and why patterns can overengineer.
